newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin says may leave, no major decisions.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin says may leave, no major decisions.

text.p: Thailand's Finance Minister said on Monday he expects to be replaced after outgoing premier Banharn Silpa-archa quits and will not make any major policy decisions in the next few weeks.
Unelected minister Bodi Chunnananda was appointed by the prime minister to hold the key finance portfolio.

But Banharn was on Saturday forced by some key partners in his six-party coalition to declare he would resign within seven days. In exchange the partners helped stave off an opposition no-confidence motion against him in parliament on the same day.

Bodi said major policy decisions would include licensing of three new Thai commercial banks, upgrading of foreign bank representative offices into full offshore banking units, controls on foreign capital inflows, and measures to shore up the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc.
He said the process of licensing new Thai banks had been completed and names of licence winners were ready for any new finance minister to announce.
